# Input

A labeled field for a short typed value.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Accessible first</span></p>

## See it live

## When to use it

**In Accessible first:** Text answers.

- **Use it when:** A name, email, phone number or other one-line answer.
- **Not when:** Long text (textarea), or a closed choice (radio group, select or checkbox).

Instead:

- [Textarea](./textarea.md): Several lines.
- [Select](./select.md): A known list of options.

## How Accessible first uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Field label or column header</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> type.label, above the field, always visible</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A placeholder as the label</div></div><div class="cap">Labels must stay visible while typing.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] A visible label, never a placeholder as the only label. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add input
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Input reads 18 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Input's tokens to change Input alone.
